item.title: Analysis: The changing face of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox politics
item.description:
Analysis: The changing face of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox politics

ne of the most significant developments in the aftermath of the Israeli elections was the decision by United Torah Judaism (UTJ), the main ultra-Orthodox Jewish party, not to recommend Benjamin Netanyahu to form the next government. 

This marks a departure from years of close alliance between Netanyahu and the ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, parties, long considered a pillar of Israeli politics.

Even if the move was tactical, intended to strengthen the Haredi parties’ bargaining position, it sends an important signal, as last month’s vote exposed several significant shifts within Haredi society.

They include the declining standing of veteran political leaders, a struggle over the future of Haredi leadership, the emergence of a new political force challenging established conventions from within, and a deepening crisis surrounding the model of the “society of learners”.

The trauma of the Hamas-led 7 October attack may have bypassed the Haredi spiritual leadership and its veteran MPs, but the wider Haredi public, including the generally more conservative Lithuanian community, understands that something momentous has happened in Israel. This is particularly true of the younger generation.

Read more: The changing face of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox politics

item.title: US Treasury chief moved to military base after alleged Iranian threats: Report
item.description:
US Treasury chief moved to military base after alleged Iranian threats: Report

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been recently moved out of his home and onto a ​military base after alleged Iranian threats against his ‌life, according to a report by the the New York Times.

In a memo seen by Reuters, a  senior intelligence official in the ​Trump administration warned that Tehran has increased efforts to  target US personnel.

The official claimed that Iranian plots against American citizens have reached "advanced stages".

item.title: ‘All I can do is hug my children and cry’: Palestinians in Gaza face deadly winter floods
item.description:
‘All I can do is hug my children and cry’: Palestinians in Gaza face deadly winter floods

On MEE Live, Palestinian journalist Nada Nabil spoke to MEE journalist James Schneider about how heavy rains and flooding are worsening conditions for displaced families in Gaza, where many are living in tents and damaged homes.

Nabil said people who would normally welcome the rain are now afraid of it. She recounted how one mother told her that all she could do was hug her children, cry and promise them better days when the sun returned.

The flooding comes as Palestinians in Gaza continue to face the consequences of Israel’s restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza.

Despite the ceasefire, Israel continues to obstruct the entry of essential supplies, including tents, blankets and materials needed to repair damaged infrastructure.

item.title: Iran denies ongoing talks with US, planned meeting in Qatar
item.description: Iran’s top security official denied on Tuesday that Tehran was holding negotiations with Washington or planning a meeting in Qatar, rejecting US claims of ongoing diplomatic contacts, Anadolu reports. Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei described US claims about continuing negotiations or a planned meeting in Qatar as “complete lies,” according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Speaking in a television interview, Rezaei accused Washington of spreading the claims to ease economic pressure and drive down oil prices. “I emphasize that we are not currently conducting any negotiations with the Americans, and there are no negotiations between us and Washington at present,” he said. item.title: Netanyahu, Trump reportedly clash over Iran in tense call: Report
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump reportedly clashed during a call over the weekend amid disagreements about the possibility of resuming military operations against Iran, media reports said Tuesday, Anadolu reports. The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, citing sources familiar with the conversation, said the call focused primarily on Iran and differences between Washington and Tel Aviv about a possible renewal of the war. Sources described the conversation as particularly difficult and confrontational, with one calling it “a screaming conversation from hell.” Netanyahu’s office, however, rejected the account, denying the conversation was contentious. “Fake news, complete nonsense,” it said in response. item.title: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot slams Netanyahu’s ‘shameful’ Knesset speech, urges Israeli emergency government
item.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Tuesday denounced caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the newly sworn-in Knesset as “shameful” and “delusional,” warning that keeping him in office endangered Israel’s security, Anadolu reports. The Yashar party leader, who has been tasked with forming the next government, accused Netanyahu of using the swearing-in ceremony of the 26th Knesset to sow division and hatred. “I became even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one minute more,” Eisenkot said in a statement. He urged the swift formation of a national emergency government, saying Netanyahu’s continued rule divides Israel and puts its security at risk.
